text: So, got into exec search, was really focused early on on consumer mobile build outs. Was doing a lot of work with Twitter and Reddit and TaskRabbit and Nextdoor, Postmates, you name it, and that was probably 85% of the work I was doing.
speaker: Lauren Ipsen
context: Lenny asks Lauren to walk through her career background and how she got to where she is now. Lauren explains her early career in executive search, describing how she worked across different industries from consumer tech companies to defense contractors. She mentions having ADD and how the variety of work kept her engaged and stimulated across multiple sectors.
text_ko: 그래서 임원 서치(exec search) 쪽으로 들어왔고, 초반에는 소비자용 모바일 확장(consumer mobile build-outs)에 정말 집중했어요. Twitter, Reddit, TaskRabbit, Nextdoor, Postmates 같은 곳들과 많이 일했고, 그런 일이 제 업무의 대략 85%였어요.
text_zh: 后来进了高管猎头（exec search）这行，早期主要集中做面向消费者的移动端扩建（build-outs）。那阵子我跟 Twitter、Reddit、TaskRabbit、Nextdoor、Postmates 这些公司合作做了很多，差不多占了我工作量的85%。
text_es: Me metí en la búsqueda de ejecutivos (exec search) y, al principio, me centré mucho en el desarrollo de productos móviles para consumidores. Trabajé bastante con Twitter, Reddit, TaskRabbit, Nextdoor, Postmates y similares; eso era como el 85% de mi trabajo.
key_sentence: was really focused early on on consumer mobile build outs.
original_text: So, got into exec search, was really focused early on on consumer mobile build outs. Was doing a lot of work with Twitter and Reddit and TaskRabbit and Nextdoor, Postmates, you name it, and that was probably 85% of the work I was doing. And then as, on the agency side, 15% was obscure, autonomous helicopters selling into the Department of Defense and then retail and robotics, and it was all very fascinating, but for me, who has wicked bad ADD, it was amazing to be able to be so stimulated by so many different industries and feel like I couldn't really master this.

vocabulary.definition: Refers to mobile technology and applications designed specifically for end-users, focusing on enhancing the consumer experience.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, consumer mobile products are developed to meet the needs of users on mobile devices, driving engagement and sales through user-friendly interfaces.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase often conveys a focus on usability and accessibility, distinguishing it from enterprise mobile solutions that target business users.

vocabulary.definition: The process of developing and expanding physical or digital infrastructure, often to accommodate growth or new services.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech companies, build outs can refer to scaling operations, such as expanding office space or enhancing software capabilities to support increased user demand.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often implies a significant investment of resources and planning, and is typically used in contexts where growth and development are prioritized.

text: I think especially for founders that haven't hired for this caliber of talent in the past, it's really easy to be distracted by shiny objects and look at huge names.
speaker: Lauren Ipsen
context: Lenny asks about the biggest mistake founders make when hiring their first senior product leader. Lauren explains that inexperienced founders often chase big names from famous companies like Google or YouTube for brand recognition, but warns this can backfire. She points out that senior executives at large companies are often removed from hands-on work and rely on their teams to execute, making them potentially less suitable for early-stage companies that need someone who can dive into tactical work.
text_ko: 특히 지금까지 이런 수준의 인재를 채용해 본 적이 없는 창업자분들은 화려한 것들에 쉽게 눈이 팔리고 유명한 이름에만 끌리기 쉬워요.
text_zh: 我觉得，尤其是那些以前没招过这种级别人才的创始人，很容易被花里胡哨的东西分心，总盯着大牌看。
text_es: Creo que, sobre todo para los fundadores que no han contratado antes talento de este nivel, suele ser muy fácil dejarse distraer por cosas llamativas (shiny objects) y fijarse en grandes nombres.
key_sentence: Founders often get distracted by shiny objects instead of this caliber of talent.
original_text: I think especially for founders that haven't hired for this caliber of talent in the past, it's really easy to be distracted by shiny objects and look at huge names. You want to find the CPOs of Google and YouTube or what have you because that seems like it would be such an incredible opportunity for brand recognition. And to an extent, it is. But the fact of the matter is, oftentimes those individuals are pretty far from the work and have a great team of executors that they've put into place that are actually the ones that are in the weeds.

vocabulary.definition: Caliber refers to the quality or level of competence of a person or thing, often measured against a standard.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, particularly in hiring, caliber is used to evaluate the skills and experience of potential candidates, ensuring they meet the company's standards.
vocabulary.nuance: While often associated with high quality, caliber can imply a comparative measure, suggesting that not all candidates are equally qualified.

vocabulary.definition: Distracted means being unable to concentrate or focus due to external stimuli or competing interests.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, being distracted can hinder decision-making and productivity, especially when leaders are sidetracked by non-essential tasks or flashy opportunities.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting a lack of discipline or focus that can lead to poor outcomes.

vocabulary.definition: Shiny objects refer to attractive but often superficial ideas or opportunities that can divert attention from more important tasks.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups, founders may encounter shiny objects in the form of trendy technologies or partnerships that seem appealing but do not align with their core objectives.
vocabulary.nuance: The phrase implies a caution against being seduced by novelty at the expense of strategic goals.

vocabulary.definition: Huge names refer to well-known, often prestigious individuals or companies that carry significant recognition and reputation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, huge names can attract attention and credibility, but relying solely on them can lead to overlooking less recognized yet equally capable candidates or opportunities.
vocabulary.nuance: While huge names can confer status, they may not always guarantee quality or fit for specific roles or projects.

text: Just because this is the best talent, that doesn't necessarily mean they are the best talent for this role today.
speaker: Lauren Ipsen
context: Lauren is discussing the importance of hiring the right person for the specific role and stage of the company, rather than just hiring the most impressive candidate on paper. She emphasizes that the best talent in general may not be the best talent for a particular role at a particular time. This follows her earlier point about founders being distracted by big names from major tech companies.
text_ko: 그 사람이 최고의 인재라고 해도, 꼭 지금 이 역할에 가장 적합하다고는 할 수 없어요.
text_zh: 就算是最优秀的人才，也不一定是现在这个岗位的最佳人选。
text_es: Solo porque alguien sea el mejor talento no significa que sea el más adecuado para este puesto en este momento.
key_sentence: that doesn't necessarily mean they are the best talent for this role today.
original_text: Just because this is the best talent, that doesn't necessarily mean they are the best talent for this role today. So to double down on that, say you are hiring and you know you're going to start hiring a senior product leader, what is it that you suggest founders nail down and iron out when they're kicking off the hiring process, either on their own or with a recruiter?

vocabulary.definition: In a way that cannot be avoided or is required; inevitably.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, 'necessarily' is often used to indicate that a conclusion or assumption may not always hold true in every situation, especially when evaluating talent or resources.
vocabulary.nuance: This term suggests that while something may be true in one context, it does not automatically apply to all cases, making it important to use it when discussing conditional outcomes.

text: Regardless of whether or not you're hiring, you should always be keeping a pulse on the market. That is the most important thing. And I think that should be the case for both candidates and folks that are hiring.
speaker: Lauren Ipsen
context: Lenny asks what founders should do when they know they will hire a head of product in the future to set themselves up for success. Lauren emphasizes the importance of always staying informed about the talent market, even when not actively hiring. She explains that both hiring managers and job candidates should maintain awareness of which companies are thriving and which individuals are performing well in their organizations.
text_ko: 채용을 하든 안 하든 항상 시장을 주시해야 해요. 그게 가장 중요해요. 지원자든 채용 담당자든 모두 마찬가지라고 생각해요.
text_zh: 不管你有没有在招人，都应该时刻关注市场动态。这才是最关键的。我觉得无论是求职者还是招聘方都应该这样做。
text_es: Da igual si estás contratando o no: siempre conviene tener el pulso del mercado. Eso es lo más importante. Y creo que eso debería valer tanto para los candidatos como para quienes contratan.
key_sentence: you should always be keeping a pulse on the market.
original_text: Regardless of whether or not you're hiring, you should always be keeping a pulse on the market. That is the most important thing. And I think that should be the case for both candidates and folks that are hiring. Like, you never want to put yourself in a position where you have no idea what good looks like, whether that's from a company standpoint or from a candidate standpoint.

vocabulary.definition: Significant in value or effect; having great meaning or influence.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, identifying important factors such as market trends or key performance indicators is crucial for strategic decision-making.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'important' conveys necessity, it can sometimes be seen as vague; using more specific terms can enhance clarity.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals being considered for a position or role, particularly in a recruitment context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In hiring processes, candidates are evaluated based on their qualifications, skills, and fit for the company culture.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'candidates' implies a competitive selection process, and is often used in formal recruitment settings rather than casual contexts.

vocabulary.definition: The process of selecting and employing individuals for specific roles within an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: Hiring is a critical function in human resources, involving various stages such as job postings, interviews, and onboarding.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'hiring' refers specifically to the act of bringing someone into a role, it can also carry implications of organizational growth and resource allocation.

text: I think breadth is incredibly important. It's so critical, especially if someone has an end goal of wanting to step into a product leadership role to have been able to have touched lots of different components, as opposed to specializing in one specific thing.
speaker: Lauren Ipsen
context: Lenny asks what product leaders and PMs should focus on to give themselves the most opportunity in their career. Lauren emphasizes the importance of gaining broad experience across different areas of product work rather than becoming overly specialized in one area. She explains this is particularly crucial for those who aspire to product leadership roles, as breadth of experience helps maximize future career opportunities.
text_ko: 저는 폭넓은 경험이 정말 중요하다고 생각해요. 특히 궁극적으로 제품 리더십(product leadership) 역할로 나아가고 싶다면, 특정 분야 하나만 파고들기보다 여러 구성 요소를 직접 다뤄본 경험이 훨씬 중요해요.
text_zh: 我觉得接触面的广度特别重要。尤其是想往产品领导岗位(product leadership role)走的人，最好能接触过很多不同的环节，而不是只专注在某一项技能上。
text_es: Creo que tener una visión amplia importa muchísimo. Es clave, sobre todo si alguien aspira a dar el salto a un rol de liderazgo de producto (product leadership role): haber trabajado en muchas áreas distintas en lugar de especializarse en una sola.
key_sentence: Breadth is critical for stepping into a product leadership role and maximizing opportunities.
original_text: I think breadth is incredibly important. It's so critical, especially if someone has an end goal of wanting to step into a product leadership role to have been able to have touched lots of different components, as opposed to specializing in one specific thing. So I would say that's very important, to be able to make sure that you're maximizing opportunities for yourself down the road.

vocabulary.definition: The extent or range of something; the width or scope of knowledge, experience, or skills.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, breadth refers to having a wide-ranging understanding of various areas, which is crucial for roles that require cross-functional collaboration and strategic decision-making.
vocabulary.nuance: While breadth is valued for its versatility, it may imply a lack of depth in any single area, which can be a disadvantage in highly specialized fields.

vocabulary.definition: Of great importance; essential for the success or functioning of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, critical often describes factors, decisions, or skills that are vital for achieving objectives or overcoming challenges.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply urgency or a high level of significance, so it should be used when emphasizing the importance of an issue or decision.

vocabulary.definition: The process of focusing on a specific area of expertise or a particular field of study or work.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, specializing allows individuals or companies to develop deep knowledge and skills in a niche area, which can lead to competitive advantages.
vocabulary.nuance: While specialization can enhance expertise, it may limit flexibility and adaptability in rapidly changing environments, making it important to balance with breadth.

vocabulary.definition: Individual parts or elements that make up a larger system or product.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, understanding the various components of a product or service is essential for effective management, development, and innovation.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often implies that each component plays a specific role in the overall functionality, highlighting the importance of integration and collaboration among different parts.

text: There's also something to be said about staying somewhere too long though. And I will say that.
speaker: Lauren Ipsen
context: Lenny asks about how often people should move between companies to optimize for future opportunities. Lauren discusses the balance between job hopping (which looks bad) and staying too long at a company. She warns against being 'loyal to a fault' when a company is clearly failing - staying at a sinking ship out of personal loyalty to the person who hired you can hurt your career in the long run.
text_ko: 다만 한자리에 너무 오래 머무르는 건 좋지 않다는 말도 있어요. 그건 제가 인정해요.
text_zh: 不过待在一个地方太久确实不太好，这点我得承认。
text_es: También hay algo que decir sobre quedarse demasiado tiempo en el mismo sitio. Y lo digo yo.
key_sentence: There's also something to be said about staying somewhere too long though.
original_text: There's also something to be said about staying somewhere too long though. And I will say that. I think sometimes you find people that are almost loyal to a fault, and companies have tanked and all executives have left and the writing's on the wall, and they're holding onto the fact that they were hired by a really good guy or gal and they want to make it work because they care about the human being, and I think sometimes in your career you do have to be a little bit more selfish and think about what's going to be best for you in the long haul.

text: So I think it's essential that you remember that this is another human being on the other end of things and that you should treat them with the same level of respect that you would expect to be treated.
speaker: Lauren Ipsen
context: Lenny asks what recruiters often do wrong when trying to attract great product talent. Lauren emphasizes that recruiters must remember they're dealing with real people, not just candidates to place. She shares her personal experience of being recruited and how transactional, impersonal recruiting calls are so off-putting that they make people want to hide their real job titles on LinkedIn to avoid being contacted by recruiters.
text_ko: 그러니까 상대방도 결국 사람이라는 걸 꼭 기억하고, 자신이 받기를 기대하는 것과 같은 존중으로 대해야 해요.
text_zh: 记住，对方也是个人，应该用你希望别人对你那样的尊重去对待他们。
text_es: Creo que es esencial que recuerdes que al otro lado hay una persona y que la trates con el mismo respeto con el que te gustaría que te trataran.
key_sentence: you should treat them with the same level of respect that you would expect to be treated.
original_text: So I think it's essential that you remember that this is another human being on the other end of things and that you should treat them with the same level of respect that you would expect to be treated. This has become even more apparent now that I have gone through some of my own recruiting cycles where I was looking for different jobs, and a transactional recruiting call just will rub you so the wrong way and will make you want to put things on your resume like I just alluded to that say things like, 'Whatever at Reddit,' or what have you because you just don't want to deal with it.

vocabulary.businessContext: In business, identifying essential elements can guide decision-making and resource allocation, ensuring that critical tasks are prioritized for success.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'essential' implies necessity, it can also suggest a foundational aspect that underpins other components or actions.

vocabulary.definition: A feeling of deep admiration for someone or something elicited by their abilities, qualities, or achievements.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate environment, fostering a culture of respect among team members can enhance collaboration and improve overall morale.
vocabulary.nuance: Respect can vary in expression; it may be formal in hierarchical settings or more casual in peer relationships, but it is always fundamental to effective communication.

vocabulary.definition: To behave toward someone in a particular way; to handle or deal with someone or something.
vocabulary.businessContext: How one treats colleagues, clients, and stakeholders can significantly impact professional relationships and the overall work environment.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'treat' can imply a level of care or consideration, and its connotation can shift based on the context, such as treating someone with kindness versus indifference.
